course.title: Cybersecurity — Beginner to Advanced
course.description: A visual-first, defensive cybersecurity course spanning security foundations, operating systems, networking, threat analysis, governance, identity, cryptography, secure software, authorized assessment, vulnerability management, SOC operations, incident response, digital forensics, cloud, IoT/OT, DevSecOps, architecture, emerging technology, and professional practice. All content is draft pending technical and editorial review.
course.version_scope: Curriculum source: Cybersecurity.pdf, Sections A-G. Official sources checked 2026-10-18 include NIST CSF 2.0, NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, OWASP Top 10:2025, OWASP API Security Top 10:2023, CIS Controls v8.1, CVSS v4.0, MITRE ATT&CK, RFC 9846 for TLS 1.3, and current official India materials. Security tools and laws change; review version/status before publication. All exercises are defensive and restricted to synthetic data, a disposable local lab, or explicitly authorized scope.
audience: students and beginners learning computing and security fundamentals
developers who want to build and review secure applications and APIs
IT practitioners interested in defensive operations, cloud security, risk, or incident response
learners considering authorized security assessment or security engineering careers
prerequisites: No previous cybersecurity experience is required; basic computer skills are sufficient. Networking, Windows/Linux, Python, and web-development familiarity becomes useful later. Use only disposable local labs or explicitly authorized targets.
learning_outcomes: Explain core security principles, threats, vulnerabilities, risk, and governance.
Interpret basic operating-system, network, identity, and cryptography concepts.
Apply practical defensive controls to synthetic datasets and authorized local labs.
Assess web/API and cloud configurations within written scope and report findings with evidence and remediation.
Investigate synthetic alerts, preserve training evidence, and outline incident response and recovery.
Design and communicate a risk-informed security improvement plan while documenting uncertainty and legal/safety boundaries.

stages.title: Foundations and safe practice
stages.goal: Explain core terms, computer and OS behavior, and networking fundamentals.
stages.milestone: Finish the terminology workbook, local permissions audit, and networking worksheet.

stages.title: Threats, governance, tools, identity and cryptography
stages.goal: Analyze threats and risks, work in isolated labs, reason about access decisions, and distinguish cryptographic properties.
stages.milestone: Produce a risk register and document safe identity and integrity checks.

stages.title: Endpoint, network, application and assessment practice
stages.goal: Design defensive controls, secure web/APIs, assess vulnerabilities, and verify remediation within scope.
stages.milestone: Complete a web/API test matrix with evidence, fixes and safe retest results.

stages.title: Security operations, response, forensics and cloud
stages.goal: Build detections, investigate synthetic incidents, preserve evidence, review cloud/device settings, and plan recovery.
stages.milestone: Deliver a documented incident investigation and recovery tabletop.

stages.title: DevSecOps, intelligence, architecture, specializations and professional practice
stages.goal: Integrate release controls, contextualize threat intelligence, design resilient architecture, assess emerging technologies, and communicate findings.
stages.milestone: Complete the Enterprise Cybersecurity Defense Platform capstone review.

dependency_notes: Computer and operating-system fundamentals precede endpoint investigation and digital forensics.
Networking precedes advanced network security and traffic interpretation.
Identity and authentication precede advanced web/API authorization.
Basic logging precedes SIEM and detection engineering.
Cryptography fundamentals precede PKI, TLS configuration, and post-quantum migration.
Risk management precedes governance audits and security architecture decisions.
